properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 19 at 1:23AM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves. Surf of 3 to 6
feet with local sets to 7 feet. Highest surf on south and
southwest facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal
Areas.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Areas of hazardous swimming conditions. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion may occur across
south-facing beaches.
properties.instruction:
A beach hazards statement is issued when threats such as strong
rip currents...elevated surf heights...and minor tidal overflow
are possible at local beaches. Obey posted warning signs and flags
and talk to a lifeguard before swimming. Use caution when in or
near the water and always swim near a lifeguard.

highest across the Straits of Florida.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering

falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 19 at 4:09AM EDT until October 21 at 7:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Watch, up
to one foot of inundation above ground level possible in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Maryland, Maryland Beaches. In Virginia, Accomack
and Northampton Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EDT Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through
Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May, Atlantic Coastal Cape May,
Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...From 3 PM to 9 PM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional elevated high tide cycles
beyond Tuesday evening are expected with additional coastal
flood hazards likely being needed.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 19 at 2:38AM EDT until October 22 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 3 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 9 to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents, large
breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM EDT Thursday. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this morning through
this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from
shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a
swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and
back injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 19 at 2:38AM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 9 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves
expected, and strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this morning
through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be life
threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first
into the bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This is a long duration event with
uncertainty on when conditions will improve. Significant ocean
overwash impacts are expected at vulnerable oceanside areas
through multiple high tide cycles into the work week. Minor
soundside water level rises will also be possible.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation
above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9
to 14 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves expected, and
strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM EDT Thursday. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this morning through
this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Hatteras Island for multiple days. This could be
life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents

water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head
first into the bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong
longshore currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

uncertainty on when conditions will improve. Significant ocean
overwash impacts are expected at vulnerable oceanside areas
through multiple high tide cycles into the work week. Minor
soundside water level rises will also be possible.

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

conditions.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 19 at 2:34AM EDT until October 22 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and

properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 19 at 2:26AM EDT until October 22 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns and
Southeast Coastal St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM EDT Tuesday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Glacier Bay; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 18 at 8:45PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river is expected to move into the NE Gulf Coast
Monday night and continue through Tuesday. Multiple periods of heavy
rain are expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf
Coast, including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove,
Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau, Haines, and Skagway. Elevated gusty winds
are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the strongest
winds from the southwest expected late Tuesday morning into Tuesday
afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce
significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast, Northeast Gulf
Coast and Northern Inner Channels. This includes the cities of
Yakutat, Gustavus, Elfin Cove, And Pelican.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Isolated landslides are
possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Yakutat area between Monday morning and
Tuesday evening range between 4-6 inches, with greater than 8
inches possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. For Elfin
Cove, Pelican, and Gustavus, rain totals ranging between 2-4
inches, exceeding 6 inches on south to southwest facing mountains
along the outer coast, and exceeding 4 inches on south to
southwest facing mountains at elevation in Glacier Bay and around
Gustavus.

Coinciding with high rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches
per hour, elevated wind gusts greater than 40 mph are expected at
elevations greater than 500 ft.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 18 at 8:42PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continue through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Haines,
Skagway, and the two highways, periods of moderate to heavy rain
will move over the area. Total rain accumulation are expected to be
between 1.5-3.0 inches, with the heaviest rain late Tuesday morning
into Tuesday afternoon. While substantial areal flooding is not
expected at this time, isolated instances of minor ponding of water
in low lying areas is possible. Furthermore, wet snow is possibly on
the Klondike Highway near White Pass up to 3 inches, though warm
surface temperatures may hinder these snow totals.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 18 at 8:58PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Northeast winds are causing river levels on the St Johns at Astor to
rise through Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to reach
Moderate Flood Stage early Monday, and remain in this stage through
the end of this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane. At
3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 2.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Sunday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early this
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at noon EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM MIDNIGHT TONIGHT TO 10 PM AKDT MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: Tanana Flats; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued October 18 at 2:59PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8
inches possible.

* WHERE...Fairbanks North Star Borough and Nenana.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lighter snow is expected Monday with some
mixed precipitation possible. Heavier snow is possible Tuesday.
There is high uncertainty in the exact snow amounts and the
placement of the heavier snow. This detail will be crucial in
determining which spots get 6"+ and 3" or less. As of right now, we
are leaning towards the heaviest snow being towards Eielson with
lighter snow in Fairbanks and especially west of Fairbanks. A 30
mile change east or west will result in drastic differences. We
will continue to update as details become clearer.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

NWSheadline: WINTER STORM WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY MORNING THROUGH WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp; Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 18 at 2:59PM AKDT until October 22 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 18 to 36
inches expected above 2500 feet with higher amounts above pass
level and 12 to 24 inches expected below 2500 feet. Winds could
gust as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Monday to 4 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Areas of
blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Following strong southerly winds north of
Trims Camp on Monday, heavy snow is expected to build in Monday
into Tuesday and Wednesday as winds shift to being out of the
north.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

gust as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Denali Borough.

* WHEN...From Monday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

update as details become clearer.

NWSheadline: WINTER STORM WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM MONDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 5 and
10 inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to

mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heavy snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon. West
and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops quickly.
Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting 1 to 3
inches or less from this.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 12:31PM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows
may occur across south-facing beaches especially in the Long
Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...
Oklahoma...

Red River near Burkburnett affecting Wichita, Cotton, Tillman,
Jefferson and Clay Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Red River near Burkburnett.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Near bankfull conditions extend along the
Red River near Davidson... Oklahoma downstream to areas near
Burkburnett and Taylor... Oklahoma.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.7 feet
Saturday evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
